Each expectedVerdict is OV-verified-correct, not merely echoed from a model run. expectedVerdict: null means 'not yet recorded' — the integration test skips that entry until it is filled.

R2 Agro TEST certificate with OV-implanted errors — the corpus's hard-error anchor. Detection-regression tripwire: a model that only fires A9 fails this entry. Three real runs on 2026-08-04 established that all three findings (II.1 added-text-without-adjacent-stamp, I.25 tickbox, A9 signing-date-not-today) fire on every run — detection is stable — but I.25's SEVERITY is not: with the correct consignor 'afi' loaded, I.25 was observed as HARD (golden run, on main) and then as MEDIUM (live run 2); a third run with the wrong consignor 'saputo-county-milk' also read I.25 as MEDIUM (plus a separate consignor-mismatch HARD). So I.25 has swung HARD/MEDIUM even holding the consignor constant — not explained by the consignor selection alone. II.1 was HARD and A9 was MEDIUM on all three runs, so those two are pinned per-finding above; I.25 is matched with no severity constraint. Per owner's decision (2026-08-04): replaced the expectedHard/expectedMedium/expectedFlagPattern counter assertions with these per-finding matchers, because per-finding matching is strictly stronger than counter matching — today's fixed counters could be satisfied by the wrong mix of findings (e.g. a missing I.25 masked by an unrelated extra flag), whereas each named finding must independently survive here. The earlier same-day re-calibration to expectedHard: 2 / expectedMedium: 1 (recorded from the golden run alone, i.e. a single observation) is superseded by this finding-level scheme.
